mail/smtp_session#

Sending e-mail: an SMTP submission client (RFC 5321, RFC 6409).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let session = await SmtpConnecting(
    host: "smtp.example.test",
    credentials: SmtpCredentials(user: "ada", password: SecretBytes("secret")),
).session();
defer session.close();
let submission = await session.submission(
    message: message,
    sender: "ada@example.test",
    recipients: ["grace@example.test", "linus@example.test"],
);
submission.complete();               // every recipient was accepted
await session.quit();

Description#

Sending e-mail: an SMTP submission client (RFC 5321, RFC 6409).

The envelope is separate from the message. sender and recipients are what the server delivers to; the From, To, Cc and Bcc headers are not read for it. Bcc and Resent-Bcc never go out (DeliveredMail), so a Bcc recipient is one more envelope recipient. An empty sender is the null reverse path <>.

Transport security is chosen, never inferred (SmtpSecurity):

  • start_tls, the default, on port 587: the greeting and EHLO in plaintext, then STARTTLS, which the server must offer (MissingSmtpExtension otherwise), a verified TLS handshake, and a new EHLO; what the server said before TLS is forgotten.
  • implicit_tls, usually on port 465: TLS before the first byte of SMTP.
  • plaintext: no TLS at all, for a trusted or test network. It takes no credentials, so a password never crosses an unverified connection. The certificate is checked against trust (the system's roots by default) and against host, a name or an IP address. A failed handshake or check ends the connection (TlsFailure, CertificateVerificationFailed); nothing falls back to plaintext.

Authentication is AUTH PLAIN only, after TLS, when credentials are given. A server that does not offer PLAIN is MissingSmtpExtension("AUTH PLAIN"); SCRAM, LOGIN, CRAM-MD5 and OAuth are not spoken. A refusal is SmtpFailure.rejected(SmtpStep.authentication, …) and the connection is closed. The password lives in a SecretBytes and appears in no error. EHLO is required: a server that refuses it is SmtpFailure.rejected(hello), and there is no fallback to HELO.

One submission is one transaction, and a session sends any number of them, one after another. Submissions started together wait for each other, so their commands never interleave. Commands are sent one at a time, without PIPELINING. The message is prepared for what the server offers (PreparedSmtpData): 8-bit content needs 8BITMIME, and a non-ASCII header or envelope address needs SMTPUTF8, or MissingSmtpExtension is thrown before anything is sent. SIZE carries the message size, not the dot-stuffed size.

Recipients are offered one by one, and a refused one does not stop the others. DATA follows when at least one recipient was accepted; submission.complete() tells whether all were, and refusals() keeps the server's reply to each refused one. When every recipient is refused nothing is sent: SmtpFailure.rejected(SmtpStep.recipients, …) with the reply to the first. SMTP has no all-or-nothing delivery to several recipients.

A submission is the server's acceptance (a 2xx reply after the data), not delivery to a mailbox: the server has taken responsibility for the message, and it may still bounce later.

A rejection, 4xx (transient) or 5xx (permanent), is SmtpFailure.rejected with the step, code and text, and the session stays usable, except 421, which closes it. Anything else closes the session: a reply that breaks the protocol (InvalidSmtpReply, SmtpFailure.unexpected), a lost connection (SmtpFailure.disconnected), a step over timeout (SmtpFailure.timed_out), and cancellation. A failure once the message data started going out is SmtpFailure.uncertain: the server may or may not have accepted the message, so it must not be sent again blindly. Nothing is retried here.

Every step has its own timeout on the monotonic clock: connecting, the TLS handshake, each command and its reply, the data and its final reply, and QUIT. The default is five minutes, as RFC 5321 asks of most replies; it asks ten for the reply after the data.

SmtpConnecting.SmtpConnecting#

SmtpSession.SmtpSession#

SmtpSession(input is AsyncReading, output is AsyncWriting, owner is Closing, capabilities is SmtpCapabilities, prefix is @byte, timeout is Duration, clock is Timing)

Takes over input and output (closing owner) once the server is greeted, secured and signed in, with its capabilities and the bytes already read past its last reply; each step within timeout on clock. SmtpConnecting.session() makes one.

SmtpSession.submission#

async submission(message is MailMessage, sender is string, recipients is Sequencing<string>) is SmtpSubmission

Sends message to recipients with sender as the return path: MAIL FROM, RCPT TO for each recipient, DATA. The result says which recipients were accepted; see the module page for failures.

Errors#

enum SmtpFailure#

enum SmtpFailure is Error = (rejected(step is SmtpStep, code is int, text is string), unexpected(step is SmtpStep, code is int, text is string), disconnected(step is SmtpStep), timed_out(step is SmtpStep), uncertain(reason is string), closed)

What went wrong in a session: the server refused a step (rejected: 4xx is transient, 5xx permanent), answered with a code the step does not allow (unexpected), went away (disconnected) or was too slow (timed_out); the message may or may not have been accepted (uncertain); or the session is over (closed).
